  assumes a single packet was lost while others are still getting through,
  triggering fast retransmit and fast recovery. In this case, the sender
  halves its congestion window and resumes linear growth. If a retransmission
  timeout occurs, indicating more severe congestion, the sender cuts the
  window all the way back to its initial size and restarts slow start. Modern
  variants like CUBIC and BBR refine these rules using delay measurements and
  pacing, but the core goal remains balancing high throughput with fairness
  and stability.
